A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MM-GRAPH, despite the changed title and expanded scope. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original link-prediction and node-classification experiments in Tables 3–4 and modality comparisons in Figure 4. Appendix C specifies three-seed means and standard deviations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds knowledge graph completion results, completed Goodreads comparisons, image-only controls, and Macro-F1 results. This judgment does not depend on the externally attributed UniGraph results.

M1.justification: The existing MMGCN/MGAT adaptations retain dot-product decoding for link prediction and three-layer MLP classification heads. v2 explicitly describes feature concatenation but does not establish a changed procedure. MoSE and VISTA are added comparison methods; no new proposed algorithm or modification resolving the earlier memory failures is documented.

E1.justification: v2 adds MM-CoDEx-s and MM-CoDEx-m, introducing Wikipedia entity graphs with typed relations and knowledge graph completion alongside the original five product/book datasets and LP/NC tasks. The candidate datasets discussed in Appendix C are excluded, not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates MoSE and VISTA on the new knowledge graph datasets in Table 6. Appendix D.3 also adds a UniGraph versus ImageBind+SAGE comparison in Table 8, explicitly attributing its results to cited work. The original GNN and MLP comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new KGC evaluation uses inherited CoDEx splits and negatives, filters entities lacking multimodal information, and reports Hits@3 alongside MRR and Hits@1/10. VISTA explicitly uses 1vsAll evaluation. v2 also adds image-only controls and Macro-F1 evaluation. Original LP/NC splits, negative counts, and hyperparameter-search budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds image-only MLP controls to the existing text-only versus multimodal comparison across the five original datasets. This extends the modality ablation to test whether combining modalities improves upon either individual modality. The existing backbone and feature-alignment analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix D both specify three runs with different random seeds and reporting means and standard deviations. Additional result rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no increased run count or new statistical testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 replaces MMGCN/MGAT Goodreads OOM entries with numerical results while retaining all previously numerical entries in the corresponding LP/NC tables. Newly reported MGAT with ViT/T5 reaches 75.26 MRR on Goodreads-LP, exceeding SAGE's retained best of 45.61. KGC results, image-only scores, Macro-F1 results, and the UniGraph comparison add substantial further evidence.

T1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the same graph-statistic and ranking-metric definitions. Neither version presents theoretical results or proofs, and v2's added task descriptions and empirical metrics introduce no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The stated contribution expands from five LP/NC datasets and GNN benchmarking to seven datasets encompassing KGC and knowledge graph embeddings. v2 additionally claims that its visually enriched CoDEx datasets address image-access and quality deficiencies in existing multimodal knowledge graphs, while retaining the original feature-encoding and multimodal-benchmark contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds dataset-dependent late-fusion and modality-split explanations for KGE results, expands the Goodreads OCR interpretation to author information on covers, and explains excluded dataset candidates. It removes the explicit full-batch memory limitation and proposed mini-batch research direction. The audio/video availability limitation survives in the conclusion.

D1.justification: v2 removes the best-hyperparameter tables and v1's reproducibility and dataset-release/file-structure/usage sections, including direct benchmark repository and Hugging Face links; the homepage remains. It adds image-crawling and feature-concatenation details, changes the evaluator description from OGB-based to PyTorch-based, and changes Ele-fashion's stated license from MIT to Apache. General optimization settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially extends positioning toward multimodal knowledge graphs, discussing existing datasets' image-access and quality problems and adding a qualitative benchmark comparison in Table 1. CoDEx, MoSE, VISTA, MMKG surveys, GLBench, and newer multimodal graph work expand the research context beyond v1's principal comparison with text-attributed graph benchmarks.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around visual information. Dataset descriptions are consolidated, empirical discussion is organized around four research questions, and the challenges and appendix structure are substantially reorganized. Candidate-dataset and additional-results sections replace substantial reproducibility and dataset-usage material.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document to two-column layout and extensively resizes and relocates figures and tables. It adds benchmark-comparison, KGC-statistics, KGC-results, UniGraph, and Macro-F1 tables, removes the two hyperparameter tables, and redraws Figure 4 with image-only bars. Existing backbone and alignment figures are retained with exchanged numbering and rearranged placement.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical completeness through KGC coverage, completed Goodreads comparisons, and image-only controls. However, it removes substantial reproducibility documentation and does not explain how the earlier memory failures were resolved. Interpretation also fails to accommodate important new evidence: Table 5 claims conventional GNNs perform best across datasets although MGAT reaches 75.26 MRR on Goodreads-LP versus SAGE's 45.61. These substantial gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
